clue.text: Taken for granted one politician's within the law

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
an MP is a Member of Parliament; the 's just joins it to what follows
licit means lawful, permitted by law

explanation.surface: A remark about a politician who stays on the right side of the law, as everyone assumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is understood without being stated, so it is assumed rather than said.

clue.text: Around middle section of path getting jolly steep

indicators.note: the word for jolly goes around the middle letters

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine

indicators.note: the middle section of path is its central two letters

explanation.surface: Walking round the middle of a path that turns very steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective describing the path, but it is the verb, to soak. A jolly is an old nickname for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: To marinate food is to soak it in a liquid, which is what steeping means.

clue.text: Tracking down pet in hiding in wood

indicators.note: the pet and the word in are hiding inside the wood

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood
a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: Finding a pet cat that has hidden in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Locating something means finding it after a search, the same as tracking it down.

clue.text: Bread and tea given to singer

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Adelina Patti was a famous Victorian opera singer

explanation.surface: Bread and a cup of tea offered to a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapatti is an unleavened flatbread from South Asia.

clue.text: Event for Manxmen?

parts.note: the Isle of Man emblem shows three running legs joined together, so a contest for its people is jokingly imagined as one where each competitor has that many

explanation.surface: Asking which competition suits people from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, has the triskelion, three armoured legs, as its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports-day race where two runners tie adjacent legs together and run as one with a combined trio.

clue.text: If centre shifts, you get distracted

indicators.note: if the centre shifts, those letters move around

explanation.surface: Moving the middle of something leaves you flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frantic, wildly agitated, like someone driven to distraction.

clue.text: Hanoverian monarch conceals a quarrel over wall paintings

indicators.note: the monarch conceals the pieces inside him

parts.note: GRI, Georgius Rex Imperator, King George, the royal cipher of the Georges

indicators.note: over says the quarrel is turned back to front

parts.note: a tiff is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A Georgian king keeping a royal row about some murals under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the quarrel round to FFIT. GRI is the cipher of the Georges, Georgius Rex Imperator.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti are words or drawings scrawled or painted on walls.

clue.text: Miss Cass has to record sound broadcast late at night

indicators.note: sound means the words are said aloud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: Eppie Cass is the girl raised by the weaver in George Eliot's novel Silas Marner; a log is a record

explanation.surface: A young woman having to tape something sounding like a late-night programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eppie log' said aloud is the answer. The epilogue was a short religious talk that closed BBC television each night.
explanation.definitionFit: The epilogue was the brief closing item at the end of a night's broadcasting.

clue.text: It's firmly fixed on strand, among the waves

definitions.text: It's firmly fixed on strand, among the waves

parts.words: It's firmly fixed on strand, among the waves
parts.note: reads like something stuck fast on a beach amid breakers, but the strand is one of hair and the waves are a hairstyle

explanation.surface: Something lodged on the shore while the sea washes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip that holds a lock of hair firmly in place amid a curled or waved hairdo.

clue.text: Having no practical experience, march out of step with music

indicators.note: marching out of step means the letters of the word march fall out of order

parts.note: an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: A band marching raggedly, unable to keep time with the tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of step' shuffles MARCH into ARMCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic or general theorises from comfort, lacking hands-on experience.

clue.text: Producing excitement as fuel is spilt around opening

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit around the other piece
fuel that is spilt is scattered, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: Petrol slopping round a hole makes for a dramatic moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is spilt' rearranges the fuel into EFUL, which goes around the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventful time is full of happenings, the kind that stir excitement.

clue.text: Start with comment on dining-room?

definitions.meaning: to begin something, set it going, or admit someone to a society
split into four short words, this is what a diner might remark about the room where they had a meal

explanation.surface: Kicking off a conversation with a remark about where you eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a split-up pun, flagged by the question mark: IN IT I ATE, said of a dining room. 'with' only links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin or set going a process is to launch it.

clue.text: See an object producing revulsion

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, see
an gives A, the indefinite article
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Looking at some item that fills you with disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense disgust or hatred, the same feeling as revulsion.

clue.text: It reveals how the gravity of the situation affects you personally

definitions.text: It reveals how the gravity of the situation affects you personally

parts.words: It reveals how the gravity of the situation affects you personally
parts.note: sounds like a report on a crisis, but gravity is the physical force, and the device shows your weight

explanation.surface: Something that shows how a serious crisis is hitting you.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale shows how strongly the earth's pull acts on your body, that is, your weight.

clue.text: Said to refrain from using prohibited frequencies

indicators.note: said means the words are heard aloud, not spelt

parts.note: to waive a right is to refrain from using it; banned means prohibited

explanation.surface: Being told not to broadcast on outlawed radio channels.
explanation.definitionFit: A waveband is a range of radio frequencies.

clue.text: Your ills may turn out to be unreal

indicators.note: the letters may turn out differently, rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling a hypochondriac that their ailments are imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory is deceptive, a mere appearance with no reality.

clue.text: Nocturnal mammal has to fly low, having lost tail for good

indicators.note: the last letter is lost and replaced by another

parts.note: to hedgehop is to fly an aircraft very low, just over the hedges

explanation.surface: A night creature skimming low, losing its tail for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for good' looks like 'permanently', but good gives the G that replaces the last letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedgehog is a spiny insectivore that forages by night.

clue.text: White feather contained in letter GI angrily sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
contained in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A soldier furiously returning a letter with a white feather of cowardice inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'contained' into the definition, leaving the hidden-word device without its signal; 'contained in' is the indicator and the definition is 'White feather' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigrette is an egret's white plume, or an ornamental tuft of such feathers.

clue.text: Clot in leg joint's a possibility for kneelers

indicators.note: the fool is put in the joint

parts.note: the hock is the joint in an animal's hind leg; read here as plural
a clot is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A blood clot in a leg joint, of all things, as an option for worshippers who kneel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassocks are firm cushions for kneeling on in church.

clue.text: French money once needed for card game

definitions.meaning: a former French gold coin worth twenty francs
..., or nap, is a trick-taking card game

explanation.surface: Old French coins being needed to play cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses take the name of the emperor: a twenty-franc coin and a bidding game played with five cards.

clue.text: Confirm live data has been processed

indicators.note: data that has been processed has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Real-time data being run through a computer to check results.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate is to verify or ratify something as correct.

clue.text: Ridicule Ironside aroused

indicators.note: Ironside aroused is stirred up, so its letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: The TV detective Ironside stirred into mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironside was a wheelchair-using TV detective, here just a word to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Derision is scornful mockery, the same as ridicule used as a noun.

clue.text: He invests some income, excluding grant initially, in booze

indicators.note: the initials go in the drink

parts.note: beer is booze

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A man putting part of his earnings, minus a grant, into drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' looks like a deletion, but it is one of four words whose initials are used. To invest a town is to besiege it, so 'He invests' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Investing a place in the military sense means surrounding it, which is what a besieging soldier does.

clue.text: A queen amused when king disappears, bound by contract

parts.note: R stands for Regina, queen

indicators.note: when the king disappears, its letter is taken out of the other word

parts.note: tickled means amused
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A queen finding it funny once the king has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when king disappears' removes K from TICKLED, giving TICLED.
explanation.definitionFit: An articled clerk is bound by written articles, an apprenticeship contract.

clue.text: North's very cold — about zero — producing torpor

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north

indicators.note: the word for very cold goes about the zero

parts.note: arctic means extremely cold
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A northern place so freezing it leaves you sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic drug induces drowsiness or stupor, sending you into a sluggish state.

clue.text: Service is, nevertheless, no good

parts.note: even so means nevertheless

explanation.surface: A grumble that a church service is pointless anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service of the Church of England.
